# grpc-dc-proxy

<!-- @generated by grpc-dc codegen. DO NOT EDIT. -->

A supported HTTP/2 <-> DataChannel proxy. Stock gRPC
clients (grpc-java and peers, HTTP/2 over TCP) call a
grpc-dc server through this proxy; it dials the server
over WebRTC-Direct and maps every call onto the existing
grpc-dc server interface. gRPC compression is terminated
in the proxy; the DataChannel wire is uncompressed.

## Modes

| Mode | Backend | Status | Implementation | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `http2-ingress` | HTTP/2 over TCP ingress -> grpc-dc server | shipped | proxy/grpc-dc-proxy.mjs --http2 [--tls-cert/--tls-key] (Node, stdlib only) | Stock grpc-java / grpc-go / grpc-node clients (h2c or TLS) call a grpc-dc server; compression terminated in the proxy |

## Client surfaces

- **Official gRPC clients (grpc-java, grpc-go, grpc-node, ...)** — HTTP/2 over TCP (h2c or TLS) to the proxy; the proxy is the only DataChannel speaker.
- **grpc-dc server (any generated language)** — Serves over WebRTC-Direct; the proxy dials its certhash multiaddr, no signaling server.

## Run (ingress-first)

Server side — a grpc-dc server on WebRTC-Direct (the Echo
demo agent; real deployments serve their own service the
same way). It prints its certhash multiaddr:

    node proxy/grpc-dc-agent.mjs --port 4001

Proxy — HTTP/2 over TCP ingress in front of that server:

    node proxy/grpc-dc-proxy.mjs --dc-dial <multiaddr> --http2 50051

- `--dc-dial` — WebRTC-Direct multiaddr of the server
  (no signaling server; the proxy is the direct dialer).
- `--http2` — stock HTTP/2 gRPC clients call here:
  plaintext h2c, or TLS with `--tls-cert/--tls-key`.
  Scope is exactly the official gRPC transport set
  (grpc-java and peers): HTTP/2 over TCP. No HTTP/3,
  no custom framed-TCP ingress.

## Test

    node --test proxy/proxy.test.mjs     # or: make test-proxy

Starts the Echo agent on WebRTC-Direct and drives a stock
HTTP/2 client through the proxy:
unary, server-streaming, and an INVALID_ARGUMENT case.
The test also checks this spec's mode table against the
implementation (parity).
